body.statement:
Assume the hypotheses of \(\mathrm{thm:quotient-efficiency}\), \(0<V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)<\infty\), fixed \(K_{\mathrm{fold}}\), the nested-split conditions of \(\mathrm{lem:learned-projection-convergence}\), and
\[
 \sqrt nL_n\min\{r_{h,n}e_{q,2,n},r_{q,n}e_{h,2,n}\}=o(1).
\]
Then, pointwise under \(P\),
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\theta_n-\theta(P)\}
 =n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(O_i)+o_p(1)
 \ \Rightarrow\ N\{0,V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\},
\]
\(\widehat V_n/V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\to_p1\), and
\[
 P\{\theta(P)\in\mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha}\}\to1-\alpha.
\]
For a locally uniform regularity extension, fix \(T<\infty\) and a class \(\mathcal S\) of bounded DQM path scores, and write \(P_{n,t,s}=P_{t/\sqrt n,s}\).  Suppose uniformly over \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(|t|\le T\): the hypotheses of \(\mathrm{thm:quotient-efficiency}\), including tangent equality and pathwise product validity, hold at every \(P_{n,t,s}\); the construction-sample bridge and multiplier bounds defining \(d_{c,n}\) and \(d_{0,n}\), the sieve approximation \(\alpha_{J_n}\), the calibration exponential-moment and concentration bounds \(\eta_{G,n},\eta_{c,n}\), the positive-eigenvalue gap, cutoff stability, coefficient and weight envelopes, and \(\Gamma_n=o_p(1)\) all hold under \(P_{n,t,s}\); the root-\(n\) mixed-bias gauge is \(o_p(1)\); \(\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_{n,t,s})\to\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\) after transport to the fixed base space \(L^2(P)\) by the canonical likelihood-ratio isometry, and its transported squared family is uniformly integrable; and
\[
 \sup_{s,t}\left|\sqrt n\{\theta(P_{n,t,s})-\theta(P)\}-tE_P\{\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)s\}\right|\to0,
\]
\[
 \sup_{s,t}\left|\log\frac{dP_{n,t,s}^n}{dP^n}
 -\frac{t}{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^ns(O_i)+\frac{t^2}{2}E_P[s^2]\right|=o_P(1),
\]
with a uniform Lindeberg condition for \(\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_{n,t,s})\), and suppose the arrays \(P_{n,t,s}^n\) and \(P^n\) are mutually contiguous uniformly on the declared class.  Then the preceding asymptotic linear expansion, variance consistency, and centered Gaussian limit hold uniformly over \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(|t|\le T\).  In particular, the estimator is regular and locally efficient on every such uniformly controlled contiguous path class.
body.proof_tex:
For the pointwise result, write \(P_{n,k}\) for the empirical measure on \(\mathcal I_k\) and define the random function
\[
 f_k=\widehat\psi^{(-k,C\mid A)}-\theta(P)-\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}.
\]
The proved \(\mathrm{lem:learned-projection-convergence}\), using all of its displayed nested-split hypotheses, gives
\[
 \max_{k\le K_{\mathrm{fold}}}\|f_k\|_{L^2(P)}=o_p(1).                       \tag{24}
\]
By \(\mathrm{ass:training-measurability}\), \(f_k\) is measurable with respect to
\(\mathcal D_{A,k}\vee\mathcal D_{C,k}\), and the observations in \(\mathcal I_k\) are independent of that sigma-field.  By \(\mathrm{ass:heldout-signal-integrability}\), its conditional second moment is finite with probability tending to one.  Because the fold sizes are proportional to \(n\) and \(K_{\mathrm{fold}}\) is fixed, conditional variance calculation gives
\[
 E\!\left[\left.\left\{\frac{|\mathcal I_k|}{\sqrt n}(P_{n,k}-P)f_k\right\}^2
 \right|\mathcal D_{A,k}\vee\mathcal D_{C,k}\right]
 \le C\|f_k\|_2^2=o_p(1).                                                     \tag{25}
\]
Conditional Chebyshev inequality and a finite union bound therefore show
\[
 \sum_{k=1}^{K_{\mathrm{fold}}}\frac{|\mathcal I_k|}{\sqrt n}(P_{n,k}-P)f_k=o_p(1). \tag{26}
\]

We next control the conditional drift without assuming that learned signal convergence already includes it.  For one learned cell, the exact expansion (6), outcome-bridge solvability, and treatment-bridge solvability imply
\[
 P\{S_a(\widehat h,\widehat q)-S_a(h^0,q^0)\}
 =-E[I_a(\widehat q-q^0)(\widehat h-h^0)].                                    \tag{27}
\]
Indeed, the expectation of the first term in (6) is
\(E[(\widehat h-h^0)\{1-T_a^*q^0\}]=0\), and that of the second is
\(E[I_a(\widehat q-q^0)\{g_a-T_ah^0\}]=0\).  Conditioning the last term in (27) first on \((A,Z,X)\) and then on \((W,X)\), and applying Cauchy--Schwarz in the respective Hilbert spaces, yields both bounds
\[
 |E[I_a\Delta q\Delta h]|
 \le\|T_a\Delta h\|_{\mathcal G_a}\|\Delta q\|_{\mathcal G_a},
 \qquad
 |E[I_a\Delta q\Delta h]|
 \le\|\Delta h\|_{\mathcal H}\|T_a^*\Delta q\|_{\mathcal H}.             \tag{28}
\]
The weights in (21) sum to one within each arm, and their total variation is at most \(L_n\) by \(\mathrm{ass:affine-weight-envelope}\).  Thus (27)--(28), \(\mathrm{ass:outcome-residual-rate}\), \(\mathrm{ass:adjoint-residual-rate}\), and the \(L^2\) parts of \(\mathrm{ass:outcome-learning-rates}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:treatment-learning-rates}\) give
\[
 \max_k|P\widehat\psi^{(-k,C\mid A)}-\theta(P)|
 =O_p\!\left(L_n\min\{r_{h,n}e_{q,2,n},r_{q,n}e_{h,2,n}\}\right)
 =o_p(n^{-1/2}),                                                               \tag{29}
\]
where the last equality is \(\mathrm{ass:primitive-mixed-bias-rate}\).

Since the folds partition the sample, equations (26)--(29) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\theta_n-\theta(P)\}
 &=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(O_i)
 +\sum_k\frac{|\mathcal I_k|}{\sqrt n}(P_{n,k}-P)f_k
 +\sum_k\frac{|\mathcal I_k|}{\sqrt n}Pf_k\\
 &=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(O_i)+o_p(1).              \tag{30}
 \end{aligned}
\]
By \(\mathrm{thm:quotient-efficiency}\), \(E[\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}]=0\) and
\(E[\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}^2]=V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\).  The theorem assumes this variance is in \((0,\infty)\).  For every \(\epsilon>0\), dominated convergence gives
\[
 E[\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}^2\mathbf1\{|\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}|>\epsilon\sqrt n\}]\longrightarrow0.
\]
Thus the frozen \(\mathrm{lem:lindeberg-feller-central-limit}\), applied to
\(X_{ni}=n^{-1/2}\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(O_i)\) using \(\mathrm{ass:iid-sampling}\), and then Slutsky's theorem applied to (30), prove
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\theta_n-\theta(P)\}\Rightarrow N\{0,V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\}. \tag{31}
\]

For variance estimation, (24), conditional Markov inequality, and the same foldwise conditioning give
\[
 \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^nf_{k(i)}(O_i)^2=o_p(1).                                   \tag{32}
\]
Empirical Cauchy--Schwarz makes the cross term between \(f_{k(i)}(O_i)\) and
\(\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(O_i)\) negligible.  It remains only to use a law of large numbers for \(\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}^2\) under a finite first moment.  For \(M<\infty\), the average of
\(\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}^2\wedge M\) converges by Chebyshev's inequality, while Markov's inequality bounds the empirical tail probability by a constant times
\(E[\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}^2\mathbf1\{\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}^2>M\}]\), which tends to zero as \(M\to\infty\).  Therefore
\[
 \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(O_i)^2\to_pV_{\mathrm{eff}}(P).       \tag{33}
\]
Equations (30), (32), and (33) imply
\[
 \widehat V_n
 =\frac1n\sum_i\{\widehat\psi_i-\theta(P)\}^2
 -\{\widehat\theta_n-\theta(P)\}^2
 \to_pV_{\mathrm{eff}}(P).
\]
Positivity of \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\) gives ratio consistency.  Slutsky's theorem and continuity of the standard normal distribution at
\(\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\) then prove the asserted pointwise Wald coverage.

We finally prove the locally uniform extension without invoking the unresolved score-lifting question.  Let
\[
 \Xi_n=\{(s,t):s\in\mathcal S,\ |t|\le T\},\qquad
 Q_{n,\xi}=P_{n,t,s}\quad(\xi=(s,t)),
\]
and abbreviate
\(\theta_{n,\xi}=\theta(Q_{n,\xi})\),
\(\phi_{n,\xi}=\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(Q_{n,\xi})\), and
\(V_{n,\xi}=E_{Q_{n,\xi}}[\phi_{n,\xi}^2]\).
The locally uniform hypotheses explicitly require the hypotheses of
\(\mathrm{thm:quotient-efficiency}\), including tangent equality and pathwise product validity, at every \(Q_{n,\xi}\).  Thus that theorem identifies \(\phi_{n,\xi}\) as the canonical gradient at each such law; this is an assumed local-law premise, not a resolution of \(\mathrm{oeq:score-lifting-completeness}\).

Take an arbitrary deterministic sequence \(\xi_n=(s_n,t_n)\in\Xi_n\) and put \(Q_n=Q_{n,\xi_n}\).  Rerunning (6)--(23) under \(Q_n\) is legitimate because every approximation, bridge-learning, multiplier, calibration-concentration, eigenvalue-gap, cutoff, coefficient, weight, and projection-gauge hypothesis used there is assumed uniformly over \(\Xi_n\).  It yields
\[
 \max_k\|\widehat\psi_{n,k}-\theta(Q_n)-\phi_{n,\xi_n}\|_{L^2(Q_n)}=o_{Q_n}(1). \tag{34}
\]
The uniform root-\(n\) mixed-bias condition similarly makes (29) \(o_{Q_n}(n^{-1/2})\).  Conditional evaluation-fold Chebyshev applied under \(Q_n\) then repeats (25)--(30), so
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\theta_n-\theta(Q_n)\}
 =\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{n,\xi_n}(O_i)+o_{Q_n}(1).                 \tag{35}
\]
Because the sequence \(\xi_n\) was arbitrary, (35) is uniform.  More explicitly, if its remainder were not uniformly \(o_p(1)\), there would be \(\delta>0\), \(\epsilon>0\), a subsequence, and choices \(\xi_n\) on that subsequence for which its probability exceeded \(\delta\), contradicting the sequencewise conclusion just proved.  This is the contradiction form of the subsequence principle, and it also applies below.

To compare the changing gradients in one Hilbert space, let
\[
 \mathsf J_{n,\xi}f=f\sqrt{dQ_{n,\xi}/dP}:L^2(Q_{n,\xi})\longrightarrow L^2(P).
\]
It is an isometry, since
\(\|\mathsf J_{n,\xi}f\|_{L^2(P)}^2=E_{Q_{n,\xi}}[f^2]\).  The assumed uniform transported \(L^2(P)\) convergence therefore gives
\[
 \sup_{\xi\in\Xi_n}|V_{n,\xi}-V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)|\longrightarrow0.           \tag{36}
\]
Moreover, all likelihood ratios in \(\mathcal V_P\) lie between \(1-\varepsilon\) and \(1+\varepsilon\).  Hence, for every fixed \(\epsilon>0\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &E_{Q_{n,\xi}}[\phi_{n,\xi}^2\mathbf1\{|\phi_{n,\xi}|>\epsilon\sqrt n\}]\\
 &\quad\le E_P[(\mathsf J_{n,\xi}\phi_{n,\xi})^2
 \mathbf1\{|\mathsf J_{n,\xi}\phi_{n,\xi}|>\epsilon\sqrt{1-\varepsilon}\sqrt n\}],
 \end{aligned}                                                               \tag{37}
\]
which tends to zero uniformly by the assumed uniform integrability of the transported squared family; this also verifies the separately stated uniform Lindeberg condition.  For every sequence \(\xi_n\), the frozen
\(\mathrm{lem:lindeberg-feller-central-limit}\), (36), and (37) give
\[
 n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{n,\xi_n}(O_i)\Rightarrow N\{0,V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\}
 \quad\text{under }Q_{n,\xi_n}^n.                                             \tag{38}
\]
The subsequence principle again turns (38) into uniform convergence in distribution over \(\Xi_n\), for example in bounded-Lipschitz distance.  Combining it with (35) proves the asserted uniform centered Gaussian limit.

The variance proof is uniform as well.  Along every sequence \(\xi_n\), conditional Markov inequality applied to (34) gives the analogue of (32).  For the leading squares, truncate \(\phi_{n,\xi_n}^2\) at \(M\).  Chebyshev's inequality controls the bounded triangular-array average by \(M/n\), and uniform integrability in (37) controls both its empirical and population tails uniformly as \(M\to\infty\).  Thus
\[
 \sup_{\xi\in\Xi_n}Q_{n,\xi}^n
 \!\left(\left|\widehat V_n-V_{n,\xi}\right|>\epsilon\right)\longrightarrow0
 \qquad(\epsilon>0).                                                         \tag{39}
\]
Equations (36) and (39), together with \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)>0\), prove uniform ratio consistency and, with (35)--(38), uniform Wald coverage for \(\theta(Q_{n,\xi})\).

Finally, the displayed uniform LAN expansion and mutual contiguity ensure that these \(Q_{n,\xi}^n\) are the declared contiguous local experiments and that base-law and local-law negligible events are interchangeable.  The assumed target expansion gives
\[
 \sqrt n\{\theta(Q_{n,\xi})-\theta(P)\}
 =tE_P[\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)s]+o(1)                                         \tag{40}
\]
uniformly.  Consequently, under \(Q_{n,\xi}^n\), centering at \(\theta(P)\) adds the local shift in (40), while centering at the true local target \(\theta(Q_{n,\xi})\) removes it and leaves the common limit in (38).  This is regularity on the declared uniformly controlled contiguous classes.  Since \(\mathrm{thm:quotient-efficiency}\) makes each \(\phi_{n,\xi}\) canonical and (36) makes its variance converge to \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\), the attained limiting variance is the local semiparametric efficiency bound.
body.justification: Nested cross-fitting makes the evaluation-fold empirical remainder conditionally negligible, the exact primal-dual identity and root-\(n\) product condition control drift, and learned-score convergence yields asymptotic linearity. Truncation proves variance consistency under second moments, while the fixed-space transport and subsequence principle prove the locally uniform triangular-array extension.
body.gap: The theorem remains conditional on \(\mathrm{thm:quotient-efficiency}\), hence on tangent equality and pathwise product validity at each relevant law. It does not settle \(\mathrm{oeq:score-lifting-completeness}\), and its uniform conclusion is limited to the explicitly controlled bounded-score contiguous classes.
body.consumer: When those quotient and learning conditions are verified, the affine ensemble provides pointwise and locally uniform efficient standard errors and Wald coverage for the proximal bridge functional.
